stories.headline: Hassabis proposes US frontier-AI standards body modeled on FINRA, with pre-release model testing

key_facts.fact: Demis Hassabis laid out a proposal for a new US AI watchdog in a personal manifesto, 'A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age,' published Tuesday morning (July 14).
key_facts.excerpt: Hassabis, the Nobel laureate behind Gemini, lays out the plan in a personal manifesto published Tuesday morning, 'A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age.'

key_facts.fact: The body would be modeled on FINRA, the private, industry-funded watchdog that polices Wall Street under SEC oversight, funded mostly by the labs it oversees.
key_facts.excerpt: Hassabis is proposing an AI standards body modeled on FINRA (Financial Industry Regulatory Authority), the private, industry-funded watchdog that polices Wall Street under SEC oversight.

key_facts.fact: Frontier labs would initially share their models with the body voluntarily, up to 30 days before release, for safety testing of dangerous cyber, biological and 'deception' capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Frontier labs would initially share their models with the body voluntarily, up to 30 days before release, for safety testing that probes dangerous cyber, biological and 'deception' capabilities.

key_facts.fact: The rules would apply to all 'Frontier-class' models regardless of country of origin or whether they are open or closed, with qualifying benchmarks updated regularly.
key_facts.excerpt: The rules would apply to all frontier-class models, 'no matter their country of origin or whether they are open or closed' - with the qualifying benchmarks regularly updated as capabilities evolve.

key_facts.fact: Participation would start voluntary, but once the assessment process proves reliable, clearing the Standards Body could become a requirement for deployment in the US market.
key_facts.excerpt: In the initial phase, participation would be voluntary, with labs sharing models for review up to 30 days ahead of release. Hassabis expects that once the assessment process proves reliable, it could be formalised so that clearing the Standards Body becomes a requirement for deployment in the US market.

stories.headline: Anthropic study of 310K conversations shows Claude's values shift by model and language

key_facts.fact: Anthropic published research (Monday, July 13) measuring how Claude's expressed values vary, analyzing 309,815 anonymized Claude.ai conversations in which users gave a subjective task.
key_facts.excerpt: we sampled 309,815 Claude.ai conversations in which the user gave Claude a subjective task. Our sample drew equally from three models (Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7) and the 20 most common languages used on Claude.ai, giving us roughly 5,000 conversations per model-language pair.

key_facts.fact: The method compressed 3,307 previously catalogued values into 339 high-level values, then reduced them via dimensionality reduction to four interpretable axes.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's method compresses its earlier 'Values in the Wild' taxonomy - 3,307 distinct values observed in Claude's outputs - down to 339 high-level values, then reduces those to four axes using dimensionality reduction.

key_facts.fact: The four axes are Deference vs. Caution, Warmth vs. Rigor, Depth vs. Brevity, and Candor vs. Execution.
key_facts.excerpt: the company identified four key axes - Deference vs. Caution, Warmth vs. Rigor, Depth vs. Brevity, and Candor vs. Execution - that capture key behavioral patterns in Claude's responses.

key_facts.fact: Claude leans furthest toward warmth in Hindi and Arabic and furthest toward rigor in English and Russian; the axes capture roughly 15% of the variation after controlling for task, topic and the user's own values.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic reports Claude leans furthest toward warmth in Hindi and Arabic, and furthest toward rigor in English and Russian... the four axes capture roughly 15% of the variation in expressed values after controlling for task, topic and the user's own values.

key_facts.fact: The three models studied - Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6 and Opus 4.7 - are now legacy, having been superseded by Claude Opus 4.8.
key_facts.excerpt: The three models Anthropic studied - Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6 and Opus 4.7 - are all now legacy... Since then, Claude Opus 4.8 [is] the [flagship].

stories.headline: New York becomes first US state to enact a data-center moratorium via Hochul executive order

key_facts.fact: Governor Kathy Hochul signed the nation's first statewide data-center moratorium via executive order, blocking new environmental permits for data centers over 50 megawatts for up to a year.
key_facts.excerpt: The order blocks new environmental permits for data centers over 50 megawatts, which the governor's office says will give the state time to come up with the regulations needed to protect residents from rising energy prices and environmental impact.

key_facts.fact: The 50MW threshold is higher than the 20MW threshold approved by state lawmakers; Hochul's office says it is meant to prevent disruption to smaller data centers used by institutions like hospitals.
key_facts.excerpt: That's higher than the 20 megawatt threshold approved by state lawmakers... the threshold is meant to prevent disruption to smaller data centers used by institutions like hospitals.

key_facts.fact: The Senate and Assembly both passed a one-year data center moratorium that Hochul did not sign; instead she issued an executive order taking effect immediately, and has not said whether she will sign the legislature's bill.
key_facts.excerpt: The state Senate and Assembly both passed a one-year data center moratorium this year that Hochul did not sign. Instead, the governor will issue an executive order that takes effect immediately and gives more direction to state agencies.

key_facts.fact: Developers have requested grid connections for more than 30 hyperscale projects in New York, each using enough power for a small- or medium-sized city; together they would use more power than Ireland.
key_facts.excerpt: Developers have requested grid connections for more than 30 hyperscale projects, each of which would use enough power for a small- or medium-sized city. Together, they would use more power than Ireland.

key_facts.fact: The Department of Environmental Conservation was ordered not to issue permits to new data centers until a generic environmental impact statement is developed; Hochul also plans to push to repeal sales tax exemptions for large data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: Hochul also said Tuesday she plans to push the legislature to roll back sales tax exemptions for large data centers in the state when they're back in session next year.

key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. central bank may need to raise interest rates 'in the near term' if coming data show inflation continuing well above the 2% target, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said on Monday, in remarks that characterized monetary policy as being at a 'crossroads.'

key_facts.fact: Waller said core PCE inflation has climbed from 3% in December 2025 to 3.4% in May, past the point where increases can be blamed on earlier tariffs.
key_facts.excerpt: I am concerned about the elevated pace of core inflation this year, which has steadily moved up—as measured by the 12-month personal consumption expenditures (PCE) rate—from 3 percent in December 2025 to 3.4 percent in May.

key_facts.fact: He said nearly 70% of core-services categories, which make up 75% of core prices, have 3-month and 12-month inflation running over 3%.

key_facts.fact: Waller pointed to June CPI due Tuesday and PPI on Wednesday as decisive; markets were pricing about a 40% chance of a July rate hike and overwhelming odds by September.
key_facts.excerpt: Financial markets are pricing about a 40% chance of a policy-rate increase at the Fed's July meeting, and overwhelming odds of a rate hike by September.

key_facts.fact: Waller argued the Fed cannot stand by, saying 'Sternly staring at inflation until it melts before our withering gaze is not an option.'

stories.headline: New Alzheimer's drug targeting brain inflammation shows first human biomarker signal at AAIC

key_facts.fact: NeuroTherapia presented Phase 2a data on July 13 at AAIC 2026 in London for NTRX-07, an oral drug that targets the brain's immune cells via the CB2 receptor pathway rather than amyloid plaques.
key_facts.excerpt: NeuroTherapia, Inc.... will be presenting data from its recently completed Phase 2a clinical trial in Alzheimer's Disease (AD) at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference (AAIC) 2026 during the Monday July 13th poster session.

key_facts.fact: The 28-day, multicenter, randomized, double-blind trial enrolled 48 participants with mild cognitive impairment or mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's, randomized 1:1 to 90 mg/day NTRX-07 or placebo.
key_facts.excerpt: The trial was a 28-day, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study designed primarily to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of NTRX-07 in 48 participants with mild cognitive impairment or mild-to-moderate AD, randomized 1:1 to NTRX-07 (90 mg/day) or placebo.

key_facts.fact: It produced the first human evidence that a selective CB2 agonist can measurably change biomarkers of nerve damage, with neurofilament light chain stabilizing in the treated group and rising on placebo.
key_facts.excerpt: For the first time, a selective CB2 receptor agonist produced measurable anti-neuroinflammatory biomarker changes in living Alzheimer's patients. The Phase 2a data, presented Monday in a poster session at the Alzheimer's Association conference in London by Cleveland-based NeuroTherapia, Inc.

key_facts.fact: The result positions neuroinflammation-targeting as a credible complement to the amyloid-clearing drugs that have dominated Alzheimer's research for three decades.
